subject.title: Feature: Opt-in cross-channel visibility in TUI (mirror iMessage/Telegram activity)

question: Should OpenClaw add a default-off TUI cross-channel observer or mirror mode, and what transcript visibility boundary should it enforce across agents, sessions, channels, devices, and operators?
rationale: The Gateway has event primitives that could support narrower live updates, but the requested cross-channel TUI visibility changes product scope, public CLI/config surface, and sensitive transcript exposure policy.

options.title: Read-Only Observer First
options.body: Add a default-off `openclaw tui --observe` style mode that only shows authorized activity for an explicit agent/session scope and defers bidirectional channel mirroring.

options.title: Full Bidirectional Mirroring
options.body: Allow messages to appear across TUI and channel surfaces, but require explicit delivery authorization, redaction, and upgrade policy before implementation.

options.title: No Core Mirror Mode
options.body: Keep raw logs, session tailing, or a future activity timeline as the supported monitoring path and avoid core cross-channel TUI mirroring.

recommendation.title: Read-Only Observer First
recommendation.body: Add a default-off `openclaw tui --observe` style mode that only shows authorized activity for an explicit agent/session scope and defers bidirectional channel mirroring.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue combines product-scope TUI behavior, security defaults, and the landed TUI session-isolation policy that steipete carried onto current main.
